title: Best local label dominates the average
statement: Let a finite-domain constraint satisfaction problem have a nonempty multiset of constraints, with every declared variable occurring in some constraint scope. Suppose the domain is nonempty and the variable set has decidable equality. For any family of probability laws on the domain, the expected affected-constraint count at a variable is at most that count when the variable is fixed to the selected best local label.
hypotheses_covered: Every declared variable occurs in a constraint scope
The domain is finite and nonempty
The variable set has decidable equality
A family of probability laws, a variable, and its best local label
